newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares end lower in sluggish trade.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares end lower in sluggish trade.

text.p: Chilean blue chips closed a shade softer in quiet trade with investors continuing to digest the impact of the government's failure Tuesday to sell power utility Colbun to a private investor, said dealers.
The market is expected to open steady with the underlying tone remaining firm, said traders.
"I don't think this current adjustment is strong enough to point to any change in trend," said Pedro Santa Maria, finance manager at brokerage Socimer.
The selective IPSA index ended down 0.06 percent at 101.46 points.
The general IGPA index lost 0.11 percent to 5,515.6 points. Volume was 12.8 billion pesos, slightly higher than Tuesday.
Traders said the market was hurt by slides in Chilean American Depositary Receipts and by general weakness in other Latin American bourses.
The government's failure to sell a 37.5 percent stake in Colbun after rejecting the only offer it received as too low, continued to unsettle investors, said traders.
"The bolsa's still recovering from the shock of Colbun. Everyone had great hopes for the sale," said one trader.
Colbun ended down two percent at 45.7 pesos after tumbling Tuesday when the news was announced.
Other losers included generator Endesa, down 1.77 percent at 264-1/4 pesos, power investment company Enersis, down 1.17 percent at 253 pesos and telecom Telex, which shed 0.72 percent to 1,380 pesos.
Winners included winery Concha y Toro, up 1.23 percent at 165 pesos, telecom CTC, up 0.67 percent at 2,420 pesos, and fertilizer-maker Soquimich, which rose 0.42 percent to 2,380 pesos.
